title: Transparency Is Not the Same as Fairness
title_ja: 透明性と公正さは同じではない
fact_notes: 町の住宅支援制度や登場する議会はすべて架空で、政策の倫理的論点を説明するためのオリジナル教材。
英文、日本語訳、設問、辞書は独自制作。過去問は引用していない。

sentences.en: When a town council began using an automated system to rank applications for housing assistance, officials promised greater consistency.
sentences.ja: 町議会が住宅支援の申請を順位づける自動化システムを使い始めたとき、担当者はより一貫した判断を約束した。

sentences.en: Previously, residents had complained that identical circumstances sometimes produced different decisions depending on which official reviewed the paperwork.
sentences.ja: 以前、住民は同じ事情でも書類を審査する担当者によって異なる判断が下されることがあると不満を述べていた。

sentences.en: The new system applied the same numerical rules to every application, making the process appear more objective and predictable.
sentences.ja: 新しいシステムはすべての申請に同じ数値規則を適用し、手続きをより客観的で予測可能に見せた。

sentences.en: However, a standardized procedure is not necessarily a fair one, particularly when its categories overlook important differences between households.
sentences.ja: しかし、標準化された手続きが必ずしも公正とは限らず、とりわけ分類が世帯間の重要な違いを見落とす場合にはそうである。

sentences.en: An applicant caring for an elderly relative might face expenses that the official forms did not adequately represent.
sentences.ja: 高齢の親族を介護する申請者は、公式の申請書では十分に表されない費用を負担しているかもしれない。

sentences.en: The controversy therefore concerned not only the accuracy of calculations but also the values embodied in the rules themselves.
sentences.ja: したがって論争は計算の正確性だけでなく、規則そのものに組み込まれた価値観にも関わっていた。

sentences.en: Supporters of the automated system argued that publishing its criteria would resolve most objections by allowing residents to inspect them.
sentences.ja: 自動化システムの支持者は、基準を公表して住民が調べられるようにすれば、ほとんどの反対意見は解消すると主張した。

sentences.en: They believed that transparency would discourage arbitrary decisions and make unequal treatment easier to challenge.
sentences.ja: 透明性が恣意的な決定を抑え、不平等な扱いへの異議申し立てを容易にすると考えたのである。

sentences.en: For example, people could ask why their medical expenses had been assigned less weight than a different financial factor.
sentences.ja: 例えば、自分の医療費が別の経済的要素より軽く扱われた理由を住民が尋ねられる。

sentences.en: Yet knowing the mathematical formula does not guarantee that an ordinary applicant can understand its practical consequences.
sentences.ja: しかし数式を知っただけでは、一般の申請者が実際の結果を理解できる保証はない。

sentences.en: A technically complete explanation can remain inaccessible if it requires specialized knowledge or extensive time to interpret.
sentences.ja: 専門知識や長い解読時間が必要なら、技術的に完全な説明でも理解できないままになり得る。

sentences.en: Meaningful transparency therefore requires information designed for the people affected, not merely documentation prepared for engineers.
sentences.ja: したがって意味のある透明性には、技術者向けの文書だけでなく、影響を受ける人々のために設計された情報が必要である。

sentences.en: A second difficulty emerged when community groups requested access to the data used to develop the ranking system.
sentences.ja: 二つ目の難しさは、地域団体が順位づけシステムの開発に使われたデータへのアクセスを求めたときに現れた。

sentences.en: They reasonably wanted to examine whether past disadvantages had influenced which applicants appeared most deserving of assistance.
sentences.ja: 過去の不利益が、どの申請者が最も支援に値すると見なされるかに影響したか確かめたいと考えたのである。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the records contained details about family relationships, debts, and health that residents had provided in confidence.
sentences.ja: それでも記録には、住民が秘密として提供した家族関係、負債、健康状態の詳細が含まれていた。

sentences.en: Releasing all such information would expose private circumstances, even if the purpose of disclosure was to detect unfairness.
sentences.ja: そのような情報をすべて公開すれば、不公正を見つける目的であっても私的な事情をさらすことになる。

sentences.en: Officials faced a conflict between public accountability and the obligation to protect people from unnecessary exposure.
sentences.ja: 担当者は、公的な説明責任と、人々を不必要な情報公開から守る義務との衝突に直面した。

sentences.en: The dispute showed that transparency must be balanced with privacy rather than treated as an unlimited good.
sentences.ja: この議論は、透明性を無制限の善とみなすのではなく、プライバシーとの均衡が必要だと示した。

sentences.en: The council eventually invited independent reviewers to inspect the system under strict rules for handling sensitive records.
sentences.ja: 最終的に議会は、機密記録の扱いに厳格な規則を設けて、独立した審査者にシステムの検証を依頼した。

sentences.en: Reviewers examined whether the chosen factors were relevant to housing needs and whether some groups experienced unexpected disadvantages.
sentences.ja: 審査者は、選ばれた要素が住宅需要に関連しているか、また一部の集団が予期しない不利益を受けていないか調べた。

sentences.en: Instead of publishing personal files, they prepared summaries explaining the methods, limitations, and unresolved questions.
sentences.ja: 個人の記録を公開する代わりに、方法、限界、未解決の問題を説明する要約を作成した。

sentences.en: The council also created a procedure through which applicants could request reconsideration when exceptional circumstances were missing from their forms.
sentences.ja: 議会はまた、申請書に例外的な事情が記されていない場合に再考を求められる手続きも設けた。

sentences.en: This appeal mechanism acknowledged that even carefully tested rules cannot anticipate every condition encountered in everyday life.
sentences.ja: この異議申し立ての仕組みは、慎重に試された規則でも日常生活のあらゆる状況を予測できないことを認めるものであった。

sentences.en: As a result, human judgment remained part of the process, although officials were expected to explain departures from the standard rules.
sentences.ja: その結果、人間の判断も手続きに残されたが、担当者は標準規則から外れる理由を説明することを求められた。

sentences.en: Some critics warned that allowing exceptions could reintroduce precisely the inconsistency the automated system had been designed to eliminate.
sentences.ja: 批判者の中には、例外を認めれば自動化システムがなくすはずだった不一致が再び生まれると警告する人もいた。

sentences.en: Others responded that refusing all exceptions would confuse equality of procedure with fairness of outcome.
sentences.ja: 一方、すべての例外を拒めば、手続きの平等と結果の公正を混同すると反論する人もいた。

sentences.en: Both concerns deserved attention because discretion can be abused, while inflexible rules can ignore genuine needs.
sentences.ja: 裁量は乱用され得る一方、柔軟性のない規則は実際の必要を無視し得るため、双方の懸念は検討に値した。

sentences.en: The council therefore required written reasons for each exception and periodic reviews of patterns across decisions.
sentences.ja: そこで議会は、例外ごとの理由を書面で示し、決定の傾向を定期的に検証するよう求めた。

sentences.en: These safeguards did not eliminate disagreement, but they made decisions easier to question and correct.
sentences.ja: こうした安全策によって意見の相違が消えたわけではないが、決定に疑問を呈し訂正することは容易になった。

sentences.en: Fair administration emerged as an ongoing practice of justification rather than a claim that a computer had discovered perfect rules.
sentences.ja: 公正な行政は、コンピューターが完璧な規則を発見したという主張ではなく、継続的に理由を示す実践として姿を現した。

sentences.en: The town also learned that an explanation offered after rejection is not equivalent to meaningful participation before rules are adopted.
sentences.ja: 町はまた、却下後に説明を与えることは、規則を採用する前の実質的な参加と同じではないと学んだ。

sentences.en: Residents needed opportunities to discuss what counted as a housing need, which hardships deserved special attention, and how errors could be reported.
sentences.ja: 住民には、住宅の必要とは何か、どの困難に特別な注意を払うべきか、誤りをどう報告するか話し合う機会が必要だった。

sentences.en: For that reason, public meetings were redesigned to include translated information, accessible examples, and time for questions.
sentences.ja: そのため公開会議は、翻訳された情報、わかりやすい例、質問の時間を含む形に作り直された。

sentences.en: The council did not promise to adopt every suggestion, but it committed to explaining why major proposals were accepted or rejected.
sentences.ja: 議会はすべての提案を採用すると約束したわけではないが、主要な案を採否した理由を説明すると約束した。

sentences.en: Participation became a means of improving the rules rather than a ceremony held after the important choices were already fixed.
sentences.ja: 参加は重要な選択が決まった後の形式的な儀式ではなく、規則を改善する方法となった。

sentences.en: It also reminded officials that those subject to a policy may possess knowledge that technical designers do not.
sentences.ja: それはまた、政策の対象となる人々が技術設計者にはない知識を持ち得ることを担当者に思い出させた。

sentences.en: The case illustrates why ethical governance cannot be reduced to selecting the most accurate algorithm or disclosing the largest amount of data.
sentences.ja: この事例は、倫理的な統治が最も正確なアルゴリズムを選ぶことや最大量のデータを公開することに還元できない理由を示している。

sentences.en: Technical reliability matters, but institutions must also confront questions about representation, privacy, accountability, and the right to appeal.
sentences.ja: 技術的な信頼性は大切だが、制度は代表性、プライバシー、説明責任、異議申し立ての権利という問いにも向き合わなければならない。

sentences.en: A rule may be applied consistently while still producing consequences that affected people have legitimate reasons to contest.
sentences.ja: 規則が一貫して適用されても、影響を受ける人々が正当な理由で異議を唱える結果が生じることはある。

sentences.en: Conversely, decisions can remain open to revision without becoming arbitrary if the reasons for revisions are recorded and examined.
sentences.ja: 逆に、修正理由が記録・検討されれば、決定は恣意的にならずに見直し可能なままでいられる。

sentences.en: The most defensible system is therefore not one that promises to end disagreement, but one that makes disagreement informative and correctable.
sentences.ja: したがって最も擁護できる制度は、意見の相違をなくすと約束するものではなく、それを情報源とし訂正可能にする制度である。

sentences.en: Fairness is sustained through institutions willing to explain their choices and listen when those explanations prove inadequate.
sentences.ja: 公正は、選択を説明し、その説明が不十分だとわかったときに耳を傾ける制度によって維持される。

questions.prompt: What did officials initially promise?
options: More private housing for all residents.
The removal of all eligibility rules.
More consistent ranking of housing applications.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第1段落の記述から「More consistent ranking of housing applications.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: What had residents complained about before the system?
options: Similar cases could receive different decisions from different officials.
There were no forms for applications.
The council refused to use computers.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第1段落の記述から「Similar cases could receive different decisions from different officials.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: Why might standardized categories still be unfair?
options: There is no need to compare applications.
They may overlook important differences in household circumstances.
Numbers are always less accurate than memories.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第1段落の記述から「They may overlook important differences in household circumstances.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: What is the central concern raised in paragraph one?
options: Medical expenses are always the largest household cost.
The values reflected in the rules matter as well as calculation accuracy.
Calculations alone determine what households need.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第1段落の記述から「The values reflected in the rules matter as well as calculation accuracy.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: Why did supporters favor publishing the criteria?
options: To require every resident to learn programming.
To discourage arbitrary decisions and enable challenges.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第2段落の記述から「To discourage arbitrary decisions and enable challenges.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: What example of a possible challenge is mentioned?
options: Questioning the weight assigned to medical expenses.
Asking why the town has schools.
Comparing the color of application forms.
Asking who designed the council building.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第2段落の記述から「Questioning the weight assigned to medical expenses.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: Why may a published mathematical formula be insufficient?
options: Ordinary applicants may not understand its consequences.
The formula must always be kept secret.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第2段落の記述から「Ordinary applicants may not understand its consequences.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: What makes transparency meaningful according to paragraph two?
options: An unlimited amount of raw data.
Replacing all written explanations with numbers.
Explanations suited to people affected by decisions.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第2段落の記述から「Explanations suited to people affected by decisions.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: Why did community groups seek development data?
options: To publish every resident's medical history.
To investigate whether old disadvantages shaped the ranking.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第3段落の記述から「To investigate whether old disadvantages shaped the ranking.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: What makes unrestricted data release problematic?
options: It could expose confidential information about residents.
The system contains no personal information.
Public records can never be examined.
Only engineers are interested in fairness.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第3段落の記述から「It could expose confidential information about residents.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: Which two aims are in tension in paragraph three?
options: Public accountability and protection of personal privacy.
Cheaper housing and better school meals.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第3段落の記述から「Public accountability and protection of personal privacy.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: What conclusion does the privacy debate support?
options: Every record should be published without consent.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第3段落の記述から「Transparency requires limits and safeguards.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: Who was invited to inspect the ranking system?
options: Students with no access to records.
Independent reviewers under strict information rules.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第4段落の記述から「Independent reviewers under strict information rules.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: How did reviewers report their findings?
options: Through summaries of methods and unresolved issues, not private files.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第4段落の記述から「Through summaries of methods and unresolved issues, not private files.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: What additional right did applicants receive?
options: The ability to modify other people's forms.
An opportunity to request reconsideration for exceptional circumstances.
The right to avoid all application rules.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第4段落の記述から「An opportunity to request reconsideration for exceptional circumstances.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: Why was human judgment retained?
options: Rules cannot anticipate every real-life condition.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第4段落の記述から「Rules cannot anticipate every real-life condition.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: What did critics fear about allowing exceptions?
options: The loss of all personal information.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第5段落の記述から「The return of inconsistent treatment.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: How did the council respond to concerns about discretion?
options: It required written reasons and periodic reviews.
It removed all records of exceptions.
It gave one official unrestricted power.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第5段落の記述から「It required written reasons and periodic reviews.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about fair administration?
options: It involves continuing justification, not perfect rules.
It depends only on program speed.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第5段落の記述から「It involves continuing justification, not perfect rules.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: Which larger distinction is important in paragraph five?
options: A written rule cannot be examined.
Equal procedures are not always the same as fair outcomes.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第5段落の記述から「Equal procedures are not always the same as fair outcomes.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: Why were public meetings redesigned?
options: Officials wanted to eliminate every question.
All decisions had already become unchangeable.
The council wanted to make meetings shorter.
Residents needed accessible ways to discuss rules before adoption.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第6段落の記述から「Residents needed accessible ways to discuss rules before adoption.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: What knowledge may affected residents have?
options: Practical experience unavailable to technical designers.
The full source code of the automated system.
Guaranteed answers to every policy problem.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第6段落の記述から「Practical experience unavailable to technical designers.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: Which change made participation more substantive?
options: Explaining why major proposals were accepted or rejected.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第6段落の記述から「Explaining why major proposals were accepted or rejected.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: What role does participation play in the passage?
options: It helps improve the rules rather than merely celebrate decisions.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第6段落の記述から「It helps improve the rules rather than merely celebrate decisions.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: Which issue extends beyond the accuracy of an algorithm?
options: Only the cost of software licenses.
Only the appearance of official forms.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第7段落の記述から「Representation, privacy, accountability, and appeals.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: What is possible even with consistently applied rules?
options: Elimination of all need for appeals.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第7段落の記述から「Legitimate objections to harmful consequences.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: When can flexible revision avoid becoming arbitrary?
options: When no written reasons are given.
When reasons for changes are recorded and reviewed.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第7段落の記述から「When reasons for changes are recorded and reviewed.」と判断できます。

questions.prompt: What distinguishes the most defensible decision system?
options: It makes disagreement useful and enables correction.
It promises that no one will disagree.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第7段落の記述から「It makes disagreement useful and enables correction.」と判断できます。

discourse.role_ja: 標準化の長所に対して公正さの問題を示す逆接です。
基準の重みづけに異議を唱える具体例です。
検証への期待と機密保護の必要を対比します。
個人ファイル公開に代わる報告方法を述べます。
審査結果として人間の判断が残ることを示します。
理由の記録という対応に導く結論です。
市民参加をしやすくする理由を示します。
一貫した規則の危険とは逆に、柔軟な修正の条件を示します。

paraphrases.source: However, a standardized procedure is not necessarily a fair one, particularly when its categories overlook important differences between households.
paraphrases.rewrite: Using identical procedures does not always lead to just treatment.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 標準化だけでは公正さが保証されないという意味です。

paraphrases.source: Meaningful transparency therefore requires information designed for the people affected, not merely documentation prepared for engineers.
paraphrases.rewrite: Explanations must be understandable to affected residents, not only technical specialists.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 住民にもわかる説明が必要という論点です。

paraphrases.source: The dispute showed that transparency must be balanced with privacy rather than treated as an unlimited good.
paraphrases.rewrite: Openness must be weighed against the need to protect personal information.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 透明性と個人情報保護の均衡を述べます。

paraphrases.source: This appeal mechanism acknowledged that even carefully tested rules cannot anticipate every condition encountered in everyday life.
paraphrases.rewrite: Even well-tested policies cannot foresee every unusual case.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 十分に検証した規則にも限界があるという意味です。

paraphrases.source: Fair administration emerged as an ongoing practice of justification rather than a claim that a computer had discovered perfect rules.
paraphrases.rewrite: Fair decision-making involves repeatedly providing reasons for choices.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 継続的な理由説明が公正な行政の本質という意味です。

paraphrases.source: Participation became a means of improving the rules rather than a ceremony held after the important choices were already fixed.
paraphrases.rewrite: Participation should shape policy rather than merely follow settled decisions.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 参加は決定後の形式的手続きにとどまらないという意味です。

paraphrases.source: The most defensible system is therefore not one that promises to end disagreement, but one that makes disagreement informative and correctable.
paraphrases.rewrite: The strongest institutions make disputes informative and allow decisions to be revised.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 意見の相違を学習・訂正につなげる制度という結論です。
